description: The bar chart illustrates the average change in compression performance as a function of observation probability, comparing two conditions: “Inferred Frames” (gray bars) and “Lexical Signal” (light orange bars). The horizontal axis, labeled “Observation Probability,” spans values from 0.2 to 0.9 in increments of 0.1, indicating the likelihood of observing an event. The vertical axis, labeled “Average Change Using Compression,” ranges from –3 to +2, with tick marks at integer intervals, representing the normalized change in compression efficiency relative to a baseline. For each observation probability, two adjacent bars show the performance of the two methods: “Inferred Frames” consistently yields negative values (indicating worse compression), ranging from approximately –2.8 at 0.2 to –1.5 at 0.9, while “Lexical Signal” yields positive values (indicating improved compression), ranging from about +0.3 at 0.2 to +1.9 at 0.5, then decreasing slightly to +1.6 at 0.9. The bars are grouped by observation probability, with “Inferred Frames” always on the left and “Lexical Signal” on the right within each group. The chart visually emphasizes that “Lexical Signal” consistently outperforms “Inferred Frames” across all observation probabilities, with the largest performance gap occurring at 0.5. No bars are shaded, outlined, or annotated beyond their color-coded legend.
